MGnifyR

2026-11-07

Source: vignettes/MGnifyR.qmd

Introduction

MGnifyR fetches microbiome data from MGnify, EBI’s resource for the analysis of metagenomic, metatranscriptomic and amplicon data. In MGnify,

  • a study (e.g., MGYS00005116) is a collection of samples,
  • a sample (e.g., SAMN02595037) is a biological specimen, e.g., a stool or soil sample,
  • a run (e.g., SRR1144937) is a sequencing of a sample, i.e., its reads. A sample can have multiple runs, e.g., an amplicon and a metagenome.
  • an assembly (e.g., ERZ1746131) is made of the reads of one or more runs, and
  • an analysis (e.g., MGYA00383350) is a run or an assembly processed with an MGnify pipeline. The data is fetched by analysis, so each column of the result is an analysis. A run can be analysed with multiple pipeline versions, so it can have multiple analyses. An analysis usually has one run, but some have multiple runs, e.g., runs that were analysed together.

MGnifyR returns the data as a TreeSummarizedExperiment, so that it can be analysed directly with the Orchestrating Microbiome Analysis with Bioconductor (OMA) tools. See the OMA book for analysis examples.

BiocManager::install("MGnifyR")
library(MGnifyR)

Browse studies

searchStudies() returns a table of studies. Studies can be filtered by biome, pipeline version and text search, and sorted with order. The available biomes are listed in the MGnify website.

studies <- searchStudies(
    biome = "root:Engineered:Built environment", max.hits = 10)
studies[, c("accession", "title", "biome_lineage")]

Fetch data

Give the studies, or their accessions, to fetchStudies(). The taxonomic profiles of all the studies are fetched and combined into a single TreeSummarizedExperiment. Taxa are matched across studies by their taxonomy.

tse <- fetchStudies("MGYS00005116")
#> Fetching 2 analyses one by one, because they are missing from the summary tables of studies. This can take a while.
#> The data includes analyses from multiple pipeline versions (V4.1, V5, V6). Their profiles are based on different reference databases. Consider subsetting the result of searchAnalyses() and fetching the analyses with fetchAnalyses().
tse
#> class: TreeSummarizedExperiment 
#> dim: 1014 6 
#> metadata(0):
#> assays(1): counts
#> rownames(1014): sk__Bacteria sk__Bacteria;k__;p__Acidobacteria ...
#>   sk__Eukaryota;k__Viridiplantae;p__Streptophyta;c__Magnoliopsida;o__Poales;f__Poaceae;g__Triticum
#>   sk__Eukaryota;k__Viridiplantae;p__Streptophyta;c__Magnoliopsida;o__Solanales;f__Solanaceae;g__Nicotiana;s__Nicotiana_attenuata
#> rowData names(8): superkingdom kingdom ... genus species
#> colnames(6): MGYA00383350 MGYA00383351 ... MGYA01026512 MGYA01026513
#> colData names(16): analysis_accession study_accession ...
#>   sample_updated_at abundance_table
#> reducedDimNames(0):
#> mainExpName: NULL
#> altExpNames(0):
#> rowLinks: NULL
#> rowTree: NULL
#> colLinks: NULL
#> colTree: NULL

The colData includes the accessions of the analysis, study, sample and run, the pipeline version and the other fields of the analyses in MGnify, e.g., the title of the sample (sample_sample_title). More metadata can be added from other sources: the samples in MGnify (samples = TRUE) and in BioSamples (biosamples = TRUE), and the studies (studies = TRUE). BioSamples has all the attributes of the samples, including study-specific variables, e.g., disease status or treatment. Each source needs its own requests, so they are not added by default. The data is cached, so adding a source later fetches only the new data.

tse <- fetchStudies("MGYS00005116", biosamples = TRUE, studies = TRUE)
#> Fetching 2 analyses one by one, because they are missing from the summary tables of studies. This can take a while.
#> The data includes analyses from multiple pipeline versions (V4.1, V5, V6). Their profiles are based on different reference databases. Consider subsetting the result of searchAnalyses() and fetching the analyses with fetchAnalyses().
colData(tse)[, c(
    "study_accession", "pipeline_version", "sample_accession", "run_accession",
    "study_biome_lineage")]
#> DataFrame with 6 rows and 5 columns
#>              study_accession pipeline_version sample_accession run_accession
#>                  <character>      <character>      <character>   <character>
#> MGYA00383350    MGYS00005116             V4.1     SAMN02594912    SRR1139729
#> MGYA00383351    MGYS00005116             V4.1     SAMN02595037    SRR1144937
#> MGYA00571587    MGYS00005116               V5     SAMN02594912    SRR1139729
#> MGYA00571730    MGYS00005116               V5     SAMN02595037    SRR1144937
#> MGYA01026512    MGYS00005116               V6     SAMN02595037    SRR1144937
#> MGYA01026513    MGYS00005116               V6     SAMN02594912    SRR1139729
#>                 study_biome_lineage
#>                         <character>
#> MGYA00383350 root:Engineered:Buil..
#> MGYA00383351 root:Engineered:Buil..
#> MGYA00571587 root:Engineered:Buil..
#> MGYA00571730 root:Engineered:Buil..
#> MGYA01026512 root:Engineered:Buil..
#> MGYA01026513 root:Engineered:Buil..
# Columns of each source
table(sub("_.*", "", colnames(colData(tse))))
#> 
#>  abundance   analysis   assembly biosamples experiment instrument   pipeline 
#>          1          1          1         24          1          2          1 
#>        run     sample      study 
#>          4          4         13

Pipeline versions

The taxonomies of different pipeline versions are based on different reference databases, so they might not be directly comparable. To fetch analyses of a single pipeline version, select them with searchAnalyses() as shown below.

Types of profiles

By default, small subunit rRNA ("SSU") profiles are fetched. type tells which profile is fetched, e.g., "mOTUs" for metagenomes and metatranscriptomes, large subunit rRNA ("LSU"), "UNITE", "ITSoneDB" or "PR2". Only the analyses that have the type are fetched. See ?fetchStudies for all the types.

tse_lsu <- fetchStudies("MGYS00005116", type = "LSU")
#> Fetching 5 analyses one by one, because they are missing from the summary tables of studies. This can take a while.
#> No LSU abundance table could be fetched for 3 analyses (no such table, or it could not be downloaded): 'MGYA00383350', 'MGYA00383351', 'MGYA00571587'
#> The data includes analyses from multiple pipeline versions (V5, V6). Their profiles are based on different reference databases. Consider subsetting the result of searchAnalyses() and fetching the analyses with fetchAnalyses().
tse_lsu
#> class: TreeSummarizedExperiment 
#> dim: 2 3 
#> metadata(0):
#> assays(1): counts
#> rownames(2):
#>   sk__Eukaryota;k__Fungi;p__Ascomycota;c__Saccharomycetes;o__Saccharomycetales
#>   Unclassified
#> rowData names(8): superkingdom kingdom ... genus species
#> colnames(3): MGYA00571730 MGYA01026512 MGYA01026513
#> colData names(16): analysis_accession study_accession ...
#>   sample_updated_at abundance_table
#> reducedDimNames(0):
#> mainExpName: NULL
#> altExpNames(0):
#> rowLinks: NULL
#> rowTree: NULL
#> colLinks: NULL
#> colTree: NULL

Functional profiles

Metagenomes, metatranscriptomes and assemblies also have functional profiles:

  • "InterPro", "GO" and "GO-slim": pipelines v1-v6
  • "Pfam" and "KO" (KEGG orthologs): pipelines v5-v6
  • "antiSMASH" (biosynthetic gene clusters): assemblies of pipelines v5-v6

In pipeline v6, only assemblies have functional profiles. Amplicons have no functional profiles. The rows are, e.g., GO terms, and rowData has their descriptions.

analyses <- searchAnalyses("MGYS00001442")
analyses <- analyses[1:3, ]
tse_go <- fetchAnalyses(analyses, type = "GO-slim")
head(rowData(tse_go))
#> DataFrame with 6 rows and 2 columns
#>                       description           category
#>                       <character>        <character>
#> GO:0000015 phosphopyruvate hydr.. cellular_component
#> GO:0000150   recombinase activity molecular_function
#> GO:0000160 phosphorelay signal .. biological_process
#> GO:0000166     nucleotide binding molecular_function
#> GO:0003674     molecular function molecular_function
#> GO:0003676   nucleic acid binding molecular_function

Multiple profiles

To fetch multiple types, give them all to type. The result is a MultiAssayExperiment with a TreeSummarizedExperiment for each type. The profiles are linked by the sample that was analysed, so, e.g., the taxonomic profile of an amplicon and the functional profile of a metagenome of the same sample are linked. Types that have no data are left out.

mae <- fetchAnalyses(analyses, type = c("SSU", "GO-slim", "InterPro"))
mae
#> A MultiAssayExperiment object of 3 listed
#>  experiments with user-defined names and respective classes.
#>  Containing an ExperimentList class object of length 3:
#>  [1] SSU: TreeSummarizedExperiment with 441 rows and 3 columns
#>  [2] GO-slim: TreeSummarizedExperiment with 116 rows and 3 columns
#>  [3] InterPro: TreeSummarizedExperiment with 8495 rows and 3 columns
#> Functionality:
#>  experiments() - obtain the ExperimentList instance
#>  colData() - the primary/phenotype DataFrame
#>  sampleMap() - the sample coordination DataFrame
#>  `$`, `[`, `[[` - extract colData columns, subset, or experiment
#>  *Format() - convert into a long or wide DataFrame
#>  assays() - convert ExperimentList to a SimpleList of matrices
#>  exportClass() - save data to flat files

Each profile is a TreeSummarizedExperiment, and the sample metadata is in colData.

mae[["GO-slim"]]
#> class: TreeSummarizedExperiment 
#> dim: 116 3 
#> metadata(0):
#> assays(1): counts
#> rownames(116): GO:0000015 GO:0000150 ... GO:1902494 GO:1990204
#> rowData names(2): description category
#> colnames(3): MGYA00096976 MGYA00096977 MGYA00096978
#> colData names(16): analysis_accession study_accession ...
#>   sample_updated_at abundance_table
#> reducedDimNames(0):
#> mainExpName: NULL
#> altExpNames(0):
#> rowLinks: NULL
#> rowTree: NULL
#> colLinks: NULL
#> colTree: NULL
colData(mae)
#> DataFrame with 3 rows and 8 columns
#>               study_accession sample_accession run_experiment_type
#>                   <character>      <character>         <character>
#> SAMEA53400418    MGYS00001442    SAMEA53400418         Metagenomic

Select analyses

To select specific analyses, e.g., based on sample metadata, use searchAnalyses(). It returns one row per analysis with the same columns as the colData. Filter the table and give it to fetchAnalyses().

analyses <- searchAnalyses("MGYS00005116")
analyses[, c("analysis_accession", "pipeline_version", "sample_accession")]
#>   analysis_accession pipeline_version sample_accession
#> 1       MGYA01026512               V6     SAMN02595037
#> 2       MGYA01026513               V6     SAMN02594912
#> 3       MGYA00383350             V4.1     SAMN02594912
#> 4       MGYA00383351             V4.1     SAMN02595037
#> 5       MGYA00571587               V5     SAMN02594912
#> 6       MGYA00571730               V5     SAMN02595037

analyses <- analyses[analyses[["pipeline_version"]] == "V6", ]
tse <- fetchAnalyses(analyses)
#> Fetching 2 analyses one by one, because they are missing from the summary tables of studies. This can take a while.
tse
#> class: TreeSummarizedExperiment 
#> dim: 520 2 
#> metadata(0):
#> assays(1): counts
#> rownames(520):
#>   sk__Bacteria;k__;p__Actinomycetota;c__Actinomycetes;o__Propionibacteriales;f__Propionibacteriaceae;g__Cutibacterium
#>   sk__Bacteria;k__;p__Bacillota;c__Bacilli;o__Bacillales;f__Staphylococcaceae;g__Staphylococcus
#>   ...
#>   sk__Eukaryota;k__Viridiplantae;p__Streptophyta;c__Magnoliopsida;o__Poales;f__Poaceae;g__Triticum
#>   sk__Eukaryota;k__Viridiplantae;p__Streptophyta;c__Magnoliopsida;o__Solanales;f__Solanaceae;g__Nicotiana;s__Nicotiana_attenuata
#> rowData names(8): superkingdom kingdom ... genus species
#> colnames(2): MGYA01026512 MGYA01026513
#> colData names(16): analysis_accession study_accession ...
#>   sample_updated_at abundance_table
#> reducedDimNames(0):
#> mainExpName: NULL
#> altExpNames(0):
#> rowLinks: NULL
#> rowTree: NULL
#> colLinks: NULL

A study can have several experiment types, e.g., metatranscriptomes and assemblies. Select them by experiment_type.

analyses <- searchAnalyses("MGYS00006572")
table(analyses[["experiment_type"]])
#> 
#>           Assembly Metatranscriptomic 
#>                  2                  2

analyses <- analyses[analyses[["experiment_type"]] == "Metatranscriptomic", ]
mae <- fetchAnalyses(analyses, type = c("SSU", "GO-slim"))
mae
#> A MultiAssayExperiment object of 2 listed
#>  experiments with user-defined names and respective classes.
#>  Containing an ExperimentList class object of length 2:
#>  [1] SSU: TreeSummarizedExperiment with 403 rows and 2 columns
#>  [2] GO-slim: TreeSummarizedExperiment with 116 rows and 2 columns
#> Functionality:
#>  experiments() - obtain the ExperimentList instance
#>  colData() - the primary/phenotype DataFrame
#>  sampleMap() - the sample coordination DataFrame
#>  `$`, `[`, `[[` - extract colData columns, subset, or experiment
#>  *Format() - convert into a long or wide DataFrame
#>  assays() - convert ExperimentList to a SimpleList of matrices
#>  exportClass() - save data to flat files

fetchAnalyses() also accepts analysis accessions, and searchSamples() returns the samples of studies.

The arguments samples, biosamples and studies (see Fetch data) choose the sources of metadata in searchAnalyses() too. Also the details of the analyses (analyses = TRUE), e.g., the quality control of pipeline v6, and of the assemblies (assemblies = TRUE) can be added. They need one request per analysis or assembly.

analyses <- searchAnalyses("MGYS00005116", analyses = TRUE)
table(sub("_.*", "", colnames(analyses)))

Caching and private data

Downloaded data is cached for the R session, so repeated calls are fast. To keep the cache between sessions, set a cache directory.

options(MGnifyR.cache = "path/to/cache")

Most MGnify data is public. To access private data, log in with ENA Webin credentials.

mgnifyLogin("Webin-1122334", "SecretPassword")
